# Rask

> Rask is the .NET One Person Framework: one developer builds, runs, and ships a whole product — UI,
> data, auth, background work, deployment — from a single C# codebase on one server, with SQLite as the
> production database (no PaaS, no assembled service stack, no second language). The UI is plain C#
> components (a Roslyn factory generator, scoped CSS/JS, routing) whose same code runs server-rendered
> over WebSockets, client-side on WebAssembly, or native iOS/Android (Rask.Native); markup uses generated
> factory methods + a children indexer (`Div()[Span(), "hi"]`). Batteries: the `rask` CLI, a
> `generate feature` CQRS+EF CRUD scaffolder, Rask.Cqrs, Rask.Data, production SQLite (pragmas + backup),
> auth, and `--docker` deploy.

This file helps AI coding assistants build apps with Rask. Start with the repo-root AGENTS.md
(the AI guidance shipped alongside this file) for app-authoring conventions, then the docs below.

## Docs
- [The .NET One Person Framework](docs/one-person-framework.md): the doctrine — one dev, whole product, one C# codebase on one server, SQLite-first; links the batteries + roadmap.
- [Getting started](docs/getting-started.md): install, first app, project layout.
- [Tutorial: zero to deploy](docs/tutorial/00-overview.md): a step-by-step build of a "Shop" app that adds every OPF pillar in order — scaffold (`rask new`), first DB-backed feature (`rask generate feature` writes the `AddRaskCqrs`/`AddRaskData`/`AddDbContextFactory` DI into Program.cs automatically — no manual paste — then `rask db add/update`), auth (`[Authorize]` + the `Authorize` component), background jobs (`rask g j` + `AddRaskJobs<Ctx>` + `IJobQueue`), transactional email (`rask g e` + `AddRaskMail<Ctx>` + `IMailQueue` + component bodies), cache (`AddRaskCache<Ctx>` + `ICache.GetOrCreateAsync`), domain events/outbox (`IOutboxEvent` + `AddRaskOutbox<Ctx>`), production SQLite (`UseRaskSqlite` + `AddRaskSqliteLitestream`), and `rask deploy --host --domain` to one box. 11 chapters under docs/tutorial/, each a real command + the generated code + a verify step; ch1 scaffolds with `--all-batteries` so every later chapter teaches what a pillar is FOR rather than how to wire it, ch9 = Web Push, ch10 = an /ops page over every pillar's table (then points at the built-in `Rask.Dashboard` that ships the finished version), ch11 = deploy. The finished app is committed as samples/Rask.Example.Shop (CLI-generated, browser-tested).
- [The `rask` CLI](docs/cli.md): the optional `Rask.Cli` .NET tool (`dotnet tool install -g Rask.Cli`) — a thin wrapper over the SDK whose only package reference is SQLite (for `rask db backup`). `rask new <name> [--template server|wasm|wasm-hosted|native] [--auth] [--pwa] [--cqrs] [--data] [--jobs] [--mail] [--cache] [--outbox] [--push] [--snapshots] [--ops] [--all-batteries] [--docker] [--output]` generates the project directly (the CLI owns all scaffolding — no `dotnet new`, no separate templates package), forwarding only the flags that template supports (fails fast otherwise); server is the default template; `--data` (server only, implies `--cqrs`) pre-wires a SQLite database — an empty `AppDbContext` + `AddRaskData()` + a `UseRaskSqlite` (WAL/`busy_timeout`) `AddDbContextFactory<AppDbContext>` whose connection string honours a `ConnectionStrings:App` override — so the first `rask generate feature <Name> --context AppDbContext` is immediately runnable with `rask db add`/`update`; the **battery flags** (server only) each add their package + `AddRaskX<AppDbContext>()` + the `modelBuilder.AddRaskX()` schema call — `--jobs`/`--mail`/`--cache`/`--outbox` (all imply `--data`), `--push` (implies `--pwa`; VAPID + `/_push/{key,subscribe,unsubscribe}` + a subscription store), `--snapshots` (scheduled Online-Backup-API copies; continuous Litestream backup already rides `--data`, config-gated on `Litestream:ReplicaUrl`, with `RaskLitestreamDownload=false` so builds stay offline), `--ops` (the `/_ops` operator dashboard — implies `--data`; emits an `AddAuthorization` policy for `RaskDashboardPolicies.Access` when `--auth` is on and a commented one when it isn't, because without a policy the dashboard denies everyone outside Development), and `--all-batteries` for the lot; the composed Program.cs gets the load-bearing order right (outbox registered BEFORE the DbContext factory so its interceptor joins the SaveChanges pipeline; `ApplyRaskConventions()` AFTER the entity configurations since it walks the model as it stands) and `--outbox` sets `DispatchDomainEventsInProcess = false` — leaving the in-process publisher on is a silent trap where DomainEventInterceptor clears each entity's events before OutboxInterceptor can copy them, so the outbox stays empty and delivery quietly stops being durable while every handler still runs; wasm-hosted emits a three-project `<Name>.Client` (browser-WASM SPA) + `<Name>.Server` (ASP.NET host you run/deploy) + `<Name>.Shared` (class library) solution, `--output` overrides the target directory; `rask generate <page|component|feature|job|email|cache> <Name>` (aliases `rask g`, `g f`/`g c`/`g p`/`g j`/`g e`/`g ca`) scaffolds a routed page (`Features/<Name>/<Name>Page.cs`), a component/job/email/cache (a read-through accessor owning its key + invalidation) under `Features/Shared/` (cross-cutting) or `Features/<Feature>/` with `--feature`/`-F`, or a full **CQRS + EF Core CRUD `feature`** under `Features/<Plural>/`: an encapsulated entity (private setters + static `Create`/`Update`; Guid id by default, `--id int|long`), a `DbContext` (or `--context` existing), create/update/delete commands + list/get queries each with a handler that owns the EF access (create/update carry a request object the form binds to), and list/create/edit pages that dispatch via `IDispatcher` with type-safe `Routes.*()` nav. Fields are **positional** — `rask g f Product Name:string Price:decimal` (legacy `--fields "n:type,…"` still accepted, not both); types string/int/long/decimal/double/bool/date/time/datetime/Guid(+aliases), optional with trailing `?`, string max-length via `(N)` (default 200), Id auto-added; **relationships** — a `<card> <Target> <fields…>` segment after the root scaffolds a related entity too (`rask g f Post Title:string 1:n Comment Body:text`), emitting the foreign key + navigation properties + EF mapping (`1:n`/`n:1`/`1:1`) or an implicit-join-table many-to-many (`n:n`); cardinalities `1:n 0:n n:1 n:0 1:1 0:1 n:n` (a `0` makes the FK optional); `--plural`/`--output`/`--force`/`--dry-run`; **writes the `AddRaskCqrs()`/`AddRaskData()`/`AddDbContextFactory<Ctx>()` registrations into Program.cs automatically** (idempotent; prints them as a fallback if it can't edit Program.cs) and prints `rask db add/update` migration next-steps. Finds the owning .csproj, derives the folder-based namespace, won't overwrite without `--force`, output compiles as-is; `rask db <add|remove|list|update|drop|backup|restore> [<name|file>] [--project/-p] [--startup-project/-s] [--context/-c] [--output/-o] [--remote] [--host] [--app] [--force/-f] [-- ef args]` wraps `dotnet ef` for the migration lifecycle (add/remove/list migrations, update/drop the database), resolving the project from the single .csproj at/above the CWD and installing `dotnet-ef` globally on first use if missing; `backup`/`restore` never touch EF — a file copy of a live SQLite database is NOT a backup (with WAL on, committed transactions sit in the -wal sidecar until a checkpoint, so the .db alone is torn or stale), so both go through SQLite: locally via Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's Online Backup API, remotely via `VACUUM INTO` inside a throwaway `alpine` container mounted on the app's `<slug>-data` volume, fetched with `docker cp` over the existing `docker -H ssh://` connection (nothing installed on the host; host/app default from `.rask/deploy.json`, `--host`/`--app` override, and the host string goes through the same SshTarget parser so a leading-`-` value can never reach ssh as an option). `restore` behaves like `drop` — prompts unless `--force`, refuses when there is no terminal — and `--remote` STOPS the app first and starts it after, deleting the `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars with the old file, because replacing a database under a live writer (or leaving a stale WAL beside it) yields a corrupted hybrid; `rask dev [--project] [--urls] [--launch-profile] [--open|--no-open] [--no-hot-reload] [--no-restart] [--once] [--no-banner] [-- app args]` runs `dotnet watch run`, resolving the project itself (the `.Server` host in a wasm-hosted solution; a native app is refused with the `dotnet build -t:Run -f net10.0-android` command it actually needs), setting `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development` when unset and the `HotReloadAutoRestart` MSBuild property so an edit hot reload cannot apply restarts instead of stalling on watch's interactive prompt (`--no-restart` to be asked); `--no-hot-reload` keeps watching and restarts on change (`--once` is a plain `dotnet run`). Component `Render()` bodies, scoped `.css`/`.js`, `[Route]` templates, CQRS handlers and job/outbox registrations all hot-reload; adding a type or changing a signature is a rude edit that restarts. In Development the browser shows a brief "Hot reload applied" pill and a restart reloads the page in ~250ms; `rask deploy [--host user@box] [--domain app.example.com] [--port] [--name] [--project] [--dockerfile] [--env KEY=VALUE] [--env-file] [--health-path] [--no-health-check] [--github-actions] [--dry-run] [--setup-host|--no-setup-host] [--deploy-user <name>|--no-deploy-user] [--no-firewall] [--no-harden-ssh]` builds+runs the app on a single host over SSH (every *deploy* op is `docker -H ssh://host …` — no registry/local daemon; builds on the box), remembering host/domain in `.rask/deploy.json` (never secrets); `--domain` fronts it with a shared auto-HTTPS Caddy proxy (Let's Encrypt) and deploys are zero-downtime blue-green, gated on an HTTP health check (`GET /health` — scaffolded by `rask new`; `--health-path` overrides, `--no-health-check` skips) so a container that starts but fails its probe never takes traffic, with multiple apps sharing one box (routing regenerated from each container's `rask.*` labels), no `--domain` publishes `--port` (default 8080) for your own proxy. Every deploy mounts a per-app named Docker volume for the SQLite database (`-v <slug>-data:/data` + `ConnectionStrings__App=Data Source=/data/app.db`) so the DB survives container replacement across redeploys, and stops the retiring container gracefully (SIGTERM, `docker stop -t 20`) before removing it so its Litestream replicator flushes and SQLite checkpoints the WAL (a plain `rm -f`/SIGKILL would drop the last frames); the `rask new --docker` image prepares a writable `/data` owned by the non-root runtime user (`mkdir -p /data && chown $APP_UID`), which a custom Dockerfile must replicate. **Handed a bare VPS it sets the box up first** (the one non-docker remote path — installing Docker over `docker -H ssh://` is chicken-and-egg, so setup shells out to plain `ssh`): one read-only probe reports what the box has, then after showing the list and asking once (`--setup-host` skips the prompt, required when there's no terminal; `--no-setup-host` refuses to touch the host) it installs Docker from get.docker.com, creates a non-root `deploy` login with your `authorized_keys` + docker group + NOPASSWD sudo (`--deploy-user`/`--no-deploy-user`) and rewrites the remembered host to it, enables ufw (sshd's real ports read off the box + 80/443 or `--port`, default-deny inbound; `--no-firewall`), and hardens sshd via `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-rask.conf` (`--no-harden-ssh`). Idempotent — a ready box is left alone with no prompt. Safety: nothing that can revoke access runs until a *fresh* connection (`ControlPath=none`) proves the new login drives docker; root login is only disabled once a non-root one exists; firewall+hardening run behind a `systemd-run` rollback timer on the host that reverts both after ~5min unless disarmed, so a lockout heals even if the CLI dies; and anything unprovable is skipped loudly (no sshd port readable → no firewall). `--github-actions` writes `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` (push to main → same `rask deploy`, `--no-setup-host` so CI never provisions) + prints the two `gh secret set` lines (`RASK_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY`, `RASK_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS`); host/domain come from the committed `.rask/deploy.json`. `rask info` reports CLI/SDK/OS; `rask --version`.
- [Live playground](docs/playground.md): write Rask component C# in the browser with a real IDE and see it compile + render live — Roslyn + the Rask source generator run entirely in WebAssembly (no server), the emitted component is Assembly.Load-ed and mounted as a child of the playground's own tree so its handlers/state run through the shared live session. The editor has Roslyn `CompletionService` IntelliSense and as-you-type diagnostics (CS + RASK) as inline Monaco squiggles, driven by a workspace-backed analysis path that never Emits/loads (so typing can't leak assemblies — only Run does); a left-hand gallery offers Counter / Form+validation / Todo starters (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter runs). The `samples/Rask.Example.Playground` app, published to GitHub Pages at `/rask/playground/` next to the showcase; ships untrimmed (Roslyn reads the `_framework/*.dll` back as metadata references, so WasmEnableWebcil=false; Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Features adds CompletionService), user code always runs interpreted, entry point is a `Playground : Component` in a namespace.
- [Best practices](docs/best-practices.md): production patterns + common pitfalls across components, state, forms, data, security, accessibility, performance, testing (each links the deep dive).
- [Elements & the DSL](docs/elements.md): the render surface — the primitives (`Text` HTML-encodes, `Raw` is verbatim, `Doctype`) and the `[...]` collection expression for sibling fragments; a generator-emitted factory for every HTML and SVG element; the universal props (`Id`/`Class`/`Style`/`Data`/`Role`/`TabIndex`/`Aria`, fixed attribute render order) on every tag; typed SVG components (no `Raw()`); and the full HTML-element catalog by category.
- [Routing](docs/routing.md): `[Route]`, params, `Router()`/`Outlet()`, navigation.
- [Lifecycle](docs/lifecycle.md): OnMount/OnPropsChanged/OnRendered/OnUnmount, async hooks.
- [Composition](docs/composition.md): the three component tiers (static method vs stateless vs stateful component), children, context (provide/consume), callbacks, toast messages (`IToaster` — scoped-per-session, consumed-once transient messages that survive a client-side navigation; drained by a headless `ToastOutlet`, or `Rask.Bootstrap`'s ready-made `BsToaster`), the full DOM `GlobalEventHandlers` event surface on every element (mouse/pointer/touch/wheel/focus/keyboard/clipboard/drag as typed `OnX`+`OnXAsync` pairs; Audio/Video add the `HTMLMediaElement` events), headless primitives (`VirtualizeModel<T>`), drag-and-drop.
- [Forms](docs/forms.md): binding, validation, EditContext, building form components — implement `IFormControl<T>` (Rask.Core.Forms) on a generic component and the generator synthesizes its controlled + bound factories, or use the public binding API directly (`ExpressionAccessor`/`BindingHelpers`/`RegisterFieldValidator`). `IFormControl<T>` is the framework primitive; ready-made `BsRadioGroup`/`BsCheckboxGroup`/`BsMultiSelect` typed controls now ship in the optional Rask.Bootstrap package (the samples keep copyable build-your-own versions). The Bootstrap form controls (`BsInput`/`BsTextarea`/`BsSelect`/`BsCheck`) auto-wire `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` + a `role="alert"` error region when a bound field is invalid.
- [Bootstrap (Rask.Bootstrap)](docs/bootstrap.md): optional package of typed Bootstrap 5.3 component factories (`BsButton`/`BsCard`/`BsModal`/…), zero-JS interactive components driven by the live runtime (`BsModal`/`BsOffcanvas` incl. responsive drawer/`BsAccordion`/`BsTabs`/`BsDropdown`/`BsToast`, controlled state), SPA-routed navigation (`BsNavbar`/`BsNav`/`BsNavItem`, auto-active via `NavLink`), `IFormControl<T>`-bound inputs (`BsInput`/`BsRadioGroup`/`BsCheckboxGroup`, and the data-driven combobox `BsSelect`/`BsMultiSelect` — a `.form-select` display box opening a `.dropdown-menu` listbox, with an opt-in `Filter` predicate `(item,text)=>bool` that adds a search field IN the dropdown, nullable × clear, float-when-filled label, `Native: true` for the OS `<select>`, plus hand-editable custom-popover `BsDatePicker`/`BsTimePicker`/`BsDateTimePicker` calendar/clock controls — type the value (live culture parse) or pick, zero-JS, keyboard-navigable, localized, Min/Max/Disable, optional seconds, native fallback), color modes (`BsTheme`), a typed `BsIcon`, and typed utility classes (`Bs.Join(Shadow.Sm, Margin.Bottom(4, Bp.Md))`); bundles Bootstrap 5.3.8 + Bootstrap Icons 1.13.1 as static assets, linked with `BootstrapStyles()`. The guide is one small page per component group (below); this hub page covers setup, color modes, the typed enums, the component map, and versioning.
- [Bootstrap layout](docs/bootstrap-layout.md): `BsContainer` (`.container`/`Fluid`/`FluidBelow: Bp` — fluid below the breakpoint, capped from it up), `BsRow` (`Gutter` → `.g-{0..5}`) + `BsCol` (`Span`/`Auto`/`Sm`…`Xxl` — per-breakpoint spans in the 12-unit grid that stack, e.g. `BsCol(Md: 6, Lg: 4)` → `.col-md-6 .col-lg-4`; `Auto` and `Span` are alternatives for the same unprefixed slot, so `Auto` wins if both are set, while `BsCol(Auto: true, Md: 6)` is a valid stack), and `BsStack` (`Vertical`/`Gap`/`Justify`/`Align`/`WrapItems`) — a flex row or column with a gap. `BsStack` builds on `d-flex`, NOT Bootstrap's `.vstack`/`.hstack`: neither shorthand is a superset (`.hstack` also sets `align-items:center` and `align-self:stretch`; `.vstack` also sets `flex:1 1 auto` and `align-self:stretch`), and Bootstrap ships no responsive variant of either, so `BsStack(Vertical: true, Class: Flex.Row(Bp.Md))` composes only on the `d-flex` base. `BsStack(Align: BsAlign.Center)` covers an `.hstack`'s alignment but not its `align-self:stretch` — add `Class: "align-self-stretch"` if a flex parent was stretching it. Prefer these components over raw `Div(Class: "row g-4")`/`Div(Class: "d-flex gap-2")`; the `Grid`/`Flex` utility groups remain the typed escape hatch via `Class`.
- [Bootstrap buttons & badges](docs/bootstrap-buttons.md): `BsButton`/`BsLink` (anchor-as-button)/`BsButtonGroup`/`BsBadge`/`BsCloseButton` with typed `BsColor`/`BsSize` variants.
- [Bootstrap cards, lists & tables](docs/bootstrap-cards.md): `BsCard` (+`BsCardHeader/Body/Footer/Title/Subtitle/Text/Image`), `BsListGroup`, `BsPlaceholder`, `BsTable`, `BsPagination`, `BsBreadcrumb`.
- [Data grid](docs/data-grid.md): `BsDataGrid<T>` + `BsColumn<T>` — typed columns bound to the row type, click-to-sort headers (`Sortable`/`SortKey`), client-side paging (`PageSize`), footer totals computed over every row (`Footer`/`FooterTemplate`), custom cells (`Template`), an `Empty` placeholder, and master-detail rows (`ExpandedContent`, needs `RowKey`). Zero JS; sorts/pages in memory, so page in the query for large sets.
- [Bootstrap alerts, spinners & progress](docs/bootstrap-feedback.md): dismissible `BsAlert` (controlled close), `BsSpinner`, `BsProgress`.
- [Bootstrap icons](docs/bootstrap-icons.md): the typed `BsIcon` over every Bootstrap Icons glyph via the generated `BsIconName` enum.
- [Bootstrap navbar & nav](docs/bootstrap-navigation.md): `BsNavbar`/`BsNavbarBrand`/`BsNav`/`BsNavItem` — SPA-routed, auto-active via `NavLink`, zero-JS.
- [Bootstrap modals, offcanvas & dropdowns](docs/bootstrap-overlays.md): controlled, zero-JS `BsModal` (focus-trapped, Escape-closes)/`BsOffcanvas` (responsive drawer)/`BsDropdown`; all `.dropdown-menu` popovers are re-anchored `position:fixed` while open (opt-in `data-rask-popover`) to escape overflow-clipping ancestors (plus `BsPopover`/`BsConfirmDialog`).
- [Bootstrap tabs, accordion & collapse](docs/bootstrap-disclosure.md): controlled, zero-JS `BsTabs`/`BsAccordion`/`BsCollapse`.
- [Bootstrap toasts](docs/bootstrap-toasts.md): controlled `BsToast` (stacked, auto-hidden from Rask state) and the `BsToaster` outlet that drains `IToaster` messages.
- [Bootstrap form controls](docs/bootstrap-forms.md): the `IFormControl<T>`-bound `BsInput`/`BsTextarea`/`BsCheck`/`BsRadioGroup`/`BsCheckboxGroup` + layout helpers (`BsFormGroup`/`BsFormLabel`/`BsInputGroup`); auto-wire `aria-invalid` + `aria-describedby` + a `role="alert"` error region when invalid.
- [Bootstrap selects & multiselect](docs/bootstrap-select.md): the data-driven combobox `BsSelect`/`BsMultiSelect` — a `.form-select` display box opening a `.dropdown-menu` listbox, opt-in `Filter` search field, nullable × clear, float-when-filled label, `Native` OS `<select>`; full roving-cursor keyboard model over the flat option list with `aria-activedescendant`/`role=option` (multiselect listbox is `aria-multiselectable`, Enter/Space toggle membership), opening focuses the filter and Enter/Esc/arrows stay inside the dropdown (single-select Enter picks without submitting the form), `OptionValue` projected-id binding, `OptionGroup` grouping (`<optgroup>` / `.dropdown-header`), `OptionDisabled` per-option disable (cursor skips it), and a multiselect `SelectAll` "Select all / Clear all" header.
- [Bootstrap date & time pickers](docs/bootstrap-pickers.md): hand-editable custom-popover `BsDatePicker`/`BsTimePicker`/`BsDateTimePicker` calendar/clock controls — type the value (live culture parse) or pick, zero-JS, full keyboard nav (arrows/Page/Home/End/Enter), localized, Min/Max/Disable, optional seconds column, `Labels` to translate the chrome, nullable × clear, native fallback.
- [Bootstrap utility classes](docs/bootstrap-utilities.md): typed utility-class tokens (`Shadow`/`Border`/`Margin`/`Padding`/`Display`/`Flex`/`Rounded`/`Txt`/`Font`/`Sizing`/`Position`/`Bg`) composed with `Bs.Join(Shadow.Sm, Margin.Bottom(4, Bp.Md))`, with an optional responsive `Bp` infix.
- [Building form controls](docs/building-form-controls.md): end-to-end guide to authoring a custom control with `IFormControl<T>` — the interface, a complete worked example, the default-method helpers, and the bound-vs-controlled / stateless-helper-vs-Component trade-offs.
- [HTTP & files](docs/http-and-files.md): data & file *transfer* — a DI'd `HttpClient` (constructor-injected, `BaseAddress` at the app origin; fetch in `OnMountAsync` with cancel/retry/error handling), the typed file-picker input (`Input(Type: InputType.File, OnFiles:)` + `RaskFile` metadata; multipart on Server, JS chunked reads on WASM), and `Navigator.Download` (event-handler-only; served from `/_rask/download/…` on Server, base64 to JS on WASM).
- [Data access](docs/data-access.md): EF Core + SQLite, IDbContextFactory, loading in the lifecycle, vertical slices, DDD value objects, SQLite decimal gotcha.
- [Choosing a database](docs/databases.md): SQLite is the DEFAULT and the recommendation; PostgreSQL and SQL Server are the opt-in door out of one box (`--database postgres|sqlserver`). SQL Server via `Rask.SqlServer`: `o.UseRaskSqlServer(cs, configure?)` applies SET LOCK_TIMEOUT + SET XACT_ABORT ON per connection and a CLIENT command timeout (SQL Server has NO server-side statement timeout, and no idle_in_transaction equivalent — the two provider packages match in shape, not in knobs); LockTimeout is validated below CommandTimeout. The claim is safe under locking READ COMMITTED and RCSI; under explicit SNAPSHOT isolation SQL Server raises error 3960 rather than double-claiming, which the per-cycle catch turns into retry-next-poll. `rask new --data --database postgres` scaffolds `Rask.Postgres`: `o.UseRaskPostgres(cs, configure?)` is a drop-in for `UseNpgsql` that applies production session settings on every connection open (statement_timeout=30s, lock_timeout=10s, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=1m; TimeSpan.Zero leaves one alone so a server/role setting wins) and enables Npgsql's own EnableRetryOnFailure (MaxRetryCount=6, MaxRetryDelay=30s). LockTimeout MUST be below StatementTimeout or the statement timeout always fires first and lock contention is misreported as a slow query — validated, throws. ONE package, no raw-ADO sibling (Npgsql already gives pooling + transient retry, unlike Microsoft.Data.Sqlite). The provider is chosen once at `rask new` and DETECTED thereafter from the project's PackageReference — `rask generate feature`, `rask db` and `rask deploy` all read it, so there is no second source of truth. What a non-file database LOSES (not degraded — there is no file): Litestream continuous backup, scheduled snapshots, `rask db backup`/`restore` (all refuse and name pg_dump), and the deploy's `/data` volume + auto `ConnectionStrings__App`. `--snapshots --database postgres` is a USAGE ERROR not a silent drop (a backup you believe you configured is worse than one you know you have not); `--all-batteries` just expands to what applies. `rask deploy` REFUSES a non-SQLite deploy with no `ConnectionStrings__App` env (it would otherwise start against the placeholder localhost string in Program.cs). Migrations are unchanged (`rask db add`/`update` forward to dotnet ef, provider-agnostic). MULTI-INSTANCE IS NOT SAFE ON ANY PROVIDER YET: the jobs/mail/outbox processors poll without claiming or leasing, so two instances run every job and send every email twice — run ONE instance; leased claiming is the next piece of work. Generated persistence tests use a temp file on SQLite and a uniquely-named create-and-drop database on PostgreSQL (override with RASK_TEST_DB). SQL Server is NOT shipped.
- [SQLite production pragmas](docs/sqlite.md): the opt-in `Rask.SQLite` package — applies a production SQLite pragma set (journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000, cache_size=2000 pages, mmap_size=128MiB, journal_size_limit=64MiB; temp_store opt-in) to every connection. Raw ADO.NET: `services.AddRaskSqlite(cs, configure?)` + inject `IRaskSqliteConnectionFactory`. Per-connection pragmas are re-applied on every pooled open (only journal_mode=WAL persists in the file); each option is overridable or nullable-to-skip via `SqlitePragmaOptions`. CONCURRENT WRITES: `factory.ExecuteInImmediateTransactionAsync(async (conn, ct) => …)` runs the work in a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction and acquires the write lock through the raw sqlite3 handle with the native busy handler off — the only wait is an `await Task.Delay` at a CONSTANT 1ms fair interval (not exponential backoff) that FREES the thread rather than blocking it inside native code; `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` takes the write lock up front, converting the otherwise UNRETRYABLE deferred read-then-write dead-lock into a plain waitable wait. Also `connection.BeginImmediate()` (returns a SqliteTransaction; its wait blocks the thread inside Microsoft.Data.Sqlite) and `connection.ExecuteInImmediateTransactionAsync(retry, work)`. `SqliteBusyRetryOptions` (Timeout=5s, PollInterval=1ms) via `AddRaskSqlite(cs, configure?, configureRetry?)`. Base package depends ONLY on Microsoft.Data.Sqlite and is reflection-free → works server-side, on MOBILE (Rask.Native, on-device — samples/Rask.Example.Native's Todos tab persists via SqliteTodoStore), and under trimming/AOT. NOT for the browser/WASM (single-threaded, WAL doesn't work, needs a native e_sqlite3 relink + manual whole-file persistence — the pragmas that justify this package don't apply there; use IIndexedDb/localStorage from Rask.Core.Browser, or the JS sqlite-wasm+OPFS stack for a real client-side DB; docs/sqlite.md#sqlite-in-the-browser-wasm). EF Core integration is a SEPARATE package `Rask.SQLite.EntityFrameworkCore`: `o.UseRaskSqlite(cs, configure?, configureRetry?)` (drop-in for UseSqlite; ConnectionOpened interceptor; pulls in Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Sqlite) — split out so the base stays EF-free for mobile/AOT. Passing configureRetry (even empty) registers a fair-interval `RaskSqliteExecutionStrategy` so SaveChanges/queries retry on SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED (turns busy_timeout=0 and lowers Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's command timeout so the async strategy owns the wait; each EF command still routes through the driver's synchronous busy-retry so a contended attempt can block ~1s before the strategy takes over — the raw ExecuteInImmediateTransactionAsync path has no such floor; the implicit SaveChanges transaction stays DEFERRED — wrap a read-then-write txn in BeginImmediate). Backup companion `Rask.SQLite.Litestream` (docs/sqlite.md#continuous-backup-with-litestream): managed Litestream supervisor — `services.AddRaskSqliteLitestream(o => { o.DatabasePath; o.ReplicaUrl="s3://…"|"gcs://…"|"abs://…"|"file://…"; o.ConfigPath?; o.RestoreOnStartup=true; o.ShutdownGracePeriod=10s; })` registers a hosted BackgroundService that runs `litestream replicate` for the process lifetime (graceful SIGINT flush on shutdown), plus `await app.Services.RestoreSqliteFromLitestreamAsync()` to restore from the replica before opening the DB (no-op if the file exists). Runs the litestream binary via CliWrap (set ExecutablePath if not on PATH). Single-writer only; DB on local disk not a network share; ideal for ephemeral containers / Azure App Service Linux (DB on local disk, replicate to abs://, single instance, Always On). Backup failures log Critical, never crash the app. Resolve the `LitestreamStatus` singleton to read replication liveness in code (`Current.IsReplicating`/`LastStartedAt`/`LastExitedAt`/`RestartCount`/`LastExitCode`/`LastError`) — a clean shutdown clears IsReplicating without counting a restart, so a climbing RestartCount means backups are flapping. Snapshot companion `Rask.SQLite.Snapshots` (docs/sqlite.md#scheduled-snapshots): scheduled CONSISTENT full-file backups via SQLite Online Backup API (`SqliteConnection.BackupDatabase`) — NO external binary, works on minimal/distroless + Alpine images. `services.AddRaskSqliteSnapshots(o => { DatabasePath; DestinationDirectory; Interval=6h; Retain=7; SnapshotOnStartup=false; BusyTimeout=30s; })` runs a hosted BackgroundService (PeriodicTimer) that snapshots + prunes to newest N; or inject `ISqliteSnapshotter` for on-demand `SnapshotAsync()`. Swap the `ISqliteSnapshotStore` (default DirectorySnapshotStore) for object storage; `store.ListAsync(ct)` reports what's held (name/size/timestamp, newest first, scoped to the store's search pattern) — a default interface impl returns empty, so a custom store must override it to be listable. Complements Litestream (streaming) or stands alone. Docker: mount a volume for DestinationDirectory or snapshots are lost on container removal; DB on local/named-volume not NFS/CIFS (WAL locking).
- [CQRS](docs/cqrs.md): the opt-in, standalone `Rask.Cqrs` package — a source-generated, reflection-free CQRS/mediator. IQuery<T>/ICommand/ICommand<T>/INotification + their handlers, dispatched via a single IDispatcher — DispatchAsync (one method for queries and commands, response type inferred) and PublishAsync for notifications; register with AddRaskCqrs(). Handlers are wired by a Roslyn generator (no runtime reflection, no assembly scanning, [DynamicDependency]-preserved ctors) so it publishes clean under the WASM/AOT trimmer. Pipeline behaviors (IPipelineBehavior<TRequest,TResult>, registered via AddOpenBehavior / AddBehavior) are the decorator hook for logging/validation/etc; none ship. Notifications fan out Sequential or WhenAll. Diagnostics RASK028 (ambiguous handler) / RASK029 (unregisterable handler). Depends only on Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.Abstractions.
- [Browser APIs](docs/browser-apis.md): the map of all typed Web-API wrappers (46) — shared vs WASM-only, one-shot vs subscription, with the inject-from-ctor pattern and the push/[JSInvokable] mechanism.
- [JS interop](docs/js-interop.md): scoped CSS/JS, element refs, IJSRuntime, typed browser APIs — shared (both transports) in Rask.Core.Browser ( plus the PWA APIs IWebPush/INotifications/IBadge/IWakeLock, and the all-host headless Shareable — OS share sheet, attaches data-rask-share to your element and fires navigator.share in the click gesture so it works on Server too, native-upgraded in the shell; plus the all-host GestureTrigger family — FullscreenTrigger/ScreenOrientationTrigger/EyeDropperTrigger/InstallTrigger/MediaCaptureTrigger/PictureInPictureTrigger, headless data-rask-gesture components that run activation-gated WASM-only APIs inside the click gesture so they reach the Server host declaratively); imperative in-process WASM+Native-shared in Rask.Client.Browser (IShare — code-driven share, native head backend on Native); WASM-only in Rask.Wasm.Browser (IScreenOrientation/IFullscreen/IInstallPrompt + device APIs ISerial/IUsb/IHid/IBluetooth/IMediaDevices/IEyeDropper/IPictureInPicture/IIdleDetector).
- [AOT compilation](docs/aot.md): opt-in full WASM AOT via `-p:RaskWasmAot=true` (default keeps the Mono interpreter; needs the wasm-tools workload). A reflection-free `TypedParserRegistry` seeds every BCL `IParsable` primitive and resolves route/query/form string values with no runtime generics; the RoutesGenerator auto-registers custom `IParsable` route/query param types; `RaskBinding.RegisterParsable<T>()` registers custom form-model value types; `InvokeAsync<T>` needs a `JsonSerializerContext` for custom T. Runtime builds under `IsAotCompatible` and the WASM sample under `EnableAotAnalyzer`, so every warnings-as-errors build enforces AOT-safety; the full AOT publish runs nightly. Mono WASM AOT is mixed-mode (interpreter stays), so the win is a clean bundle + faster binding, not crash-avoidance.
- [Data layer](docs/data.md): the opt-in `Rask.Data` package — a provider-agnostic DDD base for EF Core apps. `Entity<TId>` (Id + CreatedAt/UpdatedAt audit stamps + a domain-events buffer via Raise/DomainEvents/ClearDomainEvents), opt-in marker interfaces ISoftDeletable (adds DeletedAt) / IVersioned (adds an int concurrency token), and three ISaveChangesInterceptors: AuditingInterceptor (stamps timestamps, bumps Version), SoftDeleteInterceptor (rewrites a Deleted ISoftDeletable to Modified + sets DeletedAt so db.Remove soft-deletes; global query filter DeletedAt==null hides it — use IgnoreQueryFilters() to see/restore), DomainEventInterceptor (after commit, publishes each entity's INotification events via Rask.Cqrs IDispatcher.PublishAsync in a fresh scope, then clears — set RaskDataOptions.DispatchDomainEventsInProcess=false when an outbox owns delivery). Wire with services.AddRaskData() (registers the interceptors + a TimeProvider) + o.AddInterceptors(sp.GetServices<ISaveChangesInterceptor>()) on the DbContext + modelBuilder.ApplyRaskConventions() in OnModelCreating (adds the query filter + IsConcurrencyToken). Optimistic concurrency: round-trip the original Version (hidden form field) and set Entry(x).Property(e=>e.Version).OriginalValue before SaveChanges → DbUpdateConcurrencyException on a stale save. Depends on Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore + Rask.Cqrs; server-side (not WASM). The base the `rask generate feature` --soft-delete/--concurrency/--events scaffolder output builds on.
- [Transactional outbox](docs/outbox.md): the opt-in `Rask.Outbox` package — durable, crash-safe domain-event delivery on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis), the durable counterpart to Rask.Data's in-process publisher. Mark an event `IOutboxEvent` (: INotification); the `OutboxInterceptor` (SavingChanges) drains each tracked entity's IOutboxEvent domain events into `OutboxMessage` rows on the SAME context/transaction (atomic — never written for a rolled-back change), and the hosted `OutboxProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) publishes the oldest unprocessed batch via IDispatcher.PublishAsync and stamps ProcessedAt (or Attempts++/Error, retry to MaxAttempts) — at-least-once. Each message's outcome is saved on its OWN SaveChanges (not once per batch), so a row edited/deleted underneath the drain costs that one row instead of RE-PUBLISHING every event the batch already delivered; a failing poll is logged and retried rather than faulting the BackgroundService (which would stop the host). `OutboxOptions.RetentionPeriod` (default 7d, Zero=keep) purges PUBLISHED messages hourly in pages (delete-by-id, not one unbounded DELETE — the first sweep on a long-unpurged table would hold SQLite's write lock for its whole duration); dead letters have no ProcessedAt so retention can never match them. A source generator registers each IOutboxEvent type (name→Type) at module load so the drain deserializes with no runtime Type.GetType/scanning. Wire: `services.AddRaskCqrs()` + `services.AddRaskData(o => o.DispatchDomainEventsInProcess = false)` (outbox owns delivery — avoid double-dispatch) + `services.AddRaskOutbox<AppDbContext>(o => { PollInterval=5s; BatchSize=100; MaxAttempts=10; })` + `.AddInterceptors(sp.GetServices<ISaveChangesInterceptor>())` on the context + `modelBuilder.AddRaskOutbox()` in OnModelCreating (maps OutboxMessage). Same INotificationHandler<T> reacts whether delivered in-process or via the outbox. Server-side; SQLite is single-writer so it polls, WAL+busy_timeout keep reads flowing; add an EF migration for the table. MULTI-INSTANCE IS SAFE: each processor LEASES the batch it claims — one UPDATE whose predicate re-tests claimability (portable across SQLite/PostgreSQL, no SKIP LOCKED, no raw SQL), marking rows with a token + expiry (LeaseDuration, default 5m, must exceed PollInterval). A dead instance's lease simply expires and the work is claimable again — no sweeper. A lease stops one instance overwriting another's outcome; it does NOT make a side effect happen once (an instance overrunning its lease can have its row taken, and an email already sent is out) — at-least-once remains the contract. Attempts now counts attempts STARTED, not failures (the claim increments it), so a job that kills the process still reaches MaxAttempts; a first-time success shows Attempts=1. UPGRADING NEEDS A MIGRATION: `rask db add AddLeases && rask db update` — skip it and the processors throw every poll inside a catch, so the app looks healthy while doing nothing (they detect this case and log the two commands).  `rask generate feature --outbox` emits it.
- [Pillar metrics](docs/observability.md): each DB-backed pillar owns an OpenTelemetry-compatible `Meter` registered by its `AddRaskX` call — `Rask.Jobs`/`Rask.Outbox`/`Rask.Mail`, alongside the existing `Rask.Server`. Per pillar: `rask.<pillar>.processed|sent` + `.failed` (EVERY attempt, not every item) + `.deadlettered` (once, on the attempt that exhausts MaxAttempts) counters, a `.duration` histogram (ms), and `.pending`/`.deadletters` observable gauges. **`rask.*.deadletters` is the alert** — at-least-once with backoff means a pillar retrying itself to death still shows a healthy processed rate. Jobs/outbox tag by `job.type`/`message.type` (a closed set fixed at build time by the source generator); MAIL IS UNTAGGED ON PURPOSE (subject/recipient are unbounded → a time series per email). Queue-depth gauges are sampled on the processor's existing poll and ONLY while `metrics.WantsQueueDepth` (i.e. a listener subscribed) — never `COUNT(*)` inside the gauge callback, which a 1s collector would turn into continuous DB read load. `dotnet-counters monitor --counters Rask.Server,Rask.Jobs,Rask.Outbox,Rask.Mail`.
- [Batteries dashboard](docs/dashboard.md): the opt-in `Rask.Dashboard` package — an operator dashboard at `/_ops` over every DB-backed pillar's own table, no exporter or second datastore. `builder.Services.AddRaskDashboard<AppDbContext>()` (scaffolded by `rask new --ops`, included in `--all-batteries`) mounts a route chain under a `[Route("_ops")]` layout. Panels: Overview (a tile per queue + a banner the moment any dead letter exists), Queues (outbox/jobs/mail in one view split due/delayed/FAILED/processed, expand a row for its last error + stored payload), Cache (keys, sizes, expiry, expired-not-yet-swept), Logs (bounded in-memory tail of the ILogger pipeline — memory-only, gone on restart), System (SQLite pragmas read live via the open DbConnection, DB size, recurring-job schedule joined to RecurringJobState). A panel appears ONLY when its battery is BOTH registered (its options singleton resolves) AND mapped (Model.FindEntityType) — the second half catches AddRaskX() without modelBuilder.AddRaskX(), where the service resolves but every query throws. FAILED = `ProcessedAt IS NULL AND Attempts >= MaxAttempts`, the inverse of the processors' drain query (there is no status column). SECURITY IS FAIL-CLOSED: pages carry `[Authorize(Policy = RaskDashboardPolicies.Access)]` on the LAYOUT (RouteAuthorizationGuard walks the chain, so it covers every page + re-checks on in-app nav); the default policy is installed with PostConfigure<AuthorizationOptions> so call order is irrelevant and an app-defined policy always wins — undefined => open in Development (with a banner) and DENY-ALL everywhere else. ACTIONS `o.Actions` (default Safe): retry a dead letter / retry all / purge processed / evict a cache key; `RaskDashboardActions.All` adds delete-a-row and flush-the-cache. Each is ONE ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete with the guard in the WHERE clause (never a tracked entity), so the DB evaluates it at write time and the dashboard can't raise a concurrency exception; the retry guard is the inverse of the drain query, so a row in flight is invisible to it and retry is safe against a live queue with no coordination. Panels poll `RefreshInterval` (2s), compare before re-rendering (idle => no diff, no WS traffic), and the loop is BOUNDED by `MaxPollDuration` (5min, then a Resume button) because every open tab competes for SQLite's single write lock. Backup tiles are opt-in via `IDashboardBackupProbe` — referencing Rask.SQLite.Snapshots/Litestream would drag a native SQLitePCLRaw provider bundle into every consumer and tie a provider-agnostic EF dashboard to SQLite. Also adds `BsStat` to Rask.Bootstrap (tone colours the value, not the card).
- [Background jobs](docs/jobs.md): the opt-in `Rask.Jobs` package — durable background work on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). A job is a `IJob` (: Rask.Cqrs ICommand) run off the request thread by an ordinary `ICommandHandler<TJob>`. Inject `IJobQueue` and `EnqueueAsync(job)` (run asap) / `ScheduleAsync(job, delay|runAt)` (delayed) — writes one `Job` row (Type name + JSON payload + RunAt) via IDbContextFactory (its OWN transaction — not atomic with a business change; use Rask.Outbox for that). The hosted `JobProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) claims due jobs (ProcessedAt==null && Attempts<MaxAttempts && RunAt<=now, oldest first, BatchSize), dispatches each via IDispatcher.DispatchAsync((ICommand)job) in a fresh scope, stamps ProcessedAt; on failure Attempts++/Error and pushes RunAt out by exponential backoff (BaseRetryDelay×2^(n-1) capped at MaxRetryDelay) up to MaxAttempts (default 25) → then a dead letter kept for inspection; completed jobs purged after RetentionPeriod (default 7d, Zero=keep). Durable interval-recurring: `o.AddRecurring<T>(name, every, factory)` enqueues a fresh job per interval, tracked in a RecurringJobState table so a restart never double-runs it (single catch-up if overdue); read the schedule back from `JobOptions.RecurringJobs` (public `RecurringJobDefinition` Name/Interval/Factory) and join it to RecurringJobState for last-fired, or call Factory() to enqueue an off-schedule run. Each job's outcome is saved on its OWN SaveChanges (not once per batch), so a row edited/deleted underneath the drain costs that one row instead of re-running everything the batch already executed; a failing poll is logged and retried rather than faulting the BackgroundService (which would stop the host). A source generator registers each IJob type (name→Type) at module load for reflection-free rehydration. Wire: `services.AddRaskCqrs()` + `services.AddRaskJobs<AppDbContext>(o => { PollInterval; MaxAttempts; AddRecurring(...); })` + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskJobs()` in OnModelCreating (maps Job + RecurringJobState) + `rask db add AddJobs && rask db update`. Server-side. MULTI-INSTANCE IS SAFE: each processor LEASES the batch it claims — one UPDATE whose predicate re-tests claimability (portable across SQLite/PostgreSQL, no SKIP LOCKED, no raw SQL), marking rows with a token + expiry (LeaseDuration, default 5m, must exceed PollInterval). A dead instance's lease simply expires and the work is claimable again — no sweeper. A lease stops one instance overwriting another's outcome; it does NOT make a side effect happen once (an instance overrunning its lease can have its row taken, and an email already sent is out) — at-least-once remains the contract. Attempts now counts attempts STARTED, not failures (the claim increments it), so a job that kills the process still reaches MaxAttempts; a first-time success shows Attempts=1. UPGRADING NEEDS A MIGRATION: `rask db add AddLeases && rask db update` — skip it and the processors throw every poll inside a catch, so the app looks healthy while doing nothing (they detect this case and log the two commands). `rask generate job <Name>` (alias `g j`) scaffolds the IJob record + handler.
- [Transactional email](docs/mail.md): the opt-in `Rask.Mail` package — durable transactional email queued on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). Compose with a fluent `Email` builder (`Email.To(addr,name?).AndTo/.Cc/.Bcc/.ReplyTo/.From/.Subject/.Body(Component|string html)/.PlainText/.Attach`); `.Body(Component)` renders a Rask component to HTML IMMEDIATELY (Component.ToHtml()) so the persisted row is self-contained (no source generator, no Rask.Cqrs dependency — nothing is rehydrated at send time). Addresses are validated at the call site (MimeKit MailboxAddress.TryParse) so a malformed address throws on build, not after MaxAttempts. Inject `IMailQueue` and `SendAsync(email)` (asap) / `ScheduleAsync(email, delay|runAt)` (delayed) — writes one `QueuedMail` row (envelope + already-rendered HTML) via IDbContextFactory, defaulting From from MailOptions. The hosted `MailProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) claims due messages (ProcessedAt==null && Attempts<MaxAttempts && RunAt<=now, oldest first, BatchSize), delivers each via the registered `IMailSender` resolved per message from a fresh scope (so a custom scoped sender isn't captured), stamps ProcessedAt PER MESSAGE (a save failure re-sends at most that one, never the batch); on failure Attempts++/Error + exponential backoff (BaseRetryDelay×2^(n-1) capped MaxRetryDelay) up to MaxAttempts (default 10) → dead letter; a transient DB error (SQLITE_BUSY) is caught per cycle so it never faults the host; sent rows purged after RetentionPeriod (default 7d) via ExecuteDeleteAsync. `IMailSender` selection in AddRaskMail: `MailOptions.Smtp` set → `MailKitMailSender` (SMTP via MailKit); else `PickupDirectory` set → `PickupDirectoryMailSender` (writes .eml files); else `LogMailSender` — so it works ZERO-CONFIG in dev with no SMTP. Register your own IMailSender before AddRaskMail (any lifetime) to send via a provider API. Wire: `services.AddRaskMail<AppDbContext>(o => { o.From="..."; o.Smtp=new SmtpOptions{Host,Port,User,Password,Security}; o.PollInterval; o.MaxAttempts; })` + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskMail()` in OnModelCreating (maps QueuedMail) + `rask db add AddMail && rask db update`. References Rask.Core (Component.ToHtml) with PrivateAssets=all + MailKit; server-side; self-contained (no Rask.Jobs dependency). MULTI-INSTANCE IS SAFE: each processor LEASES the batch it claims — one UPDATE whose predicate re-tests claimability (portable across SQLite/PostgreSQL, no SKIP LOCKED, no raw SQL), marking rows with a token + expiry (LeaseDuration, default 5m, must exceed PollInterval). A dead instance's lease simply expires and the work is claimable again — no sweeper. A lease stops one instance overwriting another's outcome; it does NOT make a side effect happen once (an instance overrunning its lease can have its row taken, and an email already sent is out) — at-least-once remains the contract. Attempts now counts attempts STARTED, not failures (the claim increments it), so a job that kills the process still reaches MaxAttempts; a first-time success shows Attempts=1. UPGRADING NEEDS A MIGRATION: `rask db add AddLeases && rask db update` — skip it and the processors throw every poll inside a catch, so the app looks healthy while doing nothing (they detect this case and log the two commands).  `rask generate email <Name>` (alias `g e`) scaffolds an email-body component AND auto-wires it: when it finds a single `DbContext` in the project (or `--context <Name>`) it registers `AddRaskMail<Ctx>` in Program.cs and adds `modelBuilder.AddRaskMail()` to that context's OnModelCreating (idempotent), leaving only SMTP config + `rask db add/update`; with no context (or several, no flag) it prints the manual steps instead.
- [Cache](docs/cache.md): REDIS: `ICache` works over ANY IDistributedCache — `services.AddStackExchangeRedisCache(...)` then the NON-GENERIC `services.AddRaskCache()` (no <TContext>), which registers ONLY ICache: no purger, no CacheEntry table, no migration. It takes NO CacheOptions on purpose — PurgeInterval and DefaultSlidingExpiration are implemented by the EF store, so against Redis they would silently do nothing; expiry is the store's business. There is deliberately NO Rask.Cache.Redis package (Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.StackExchangeRedis is the standard API). Only the cache moves — jobs, mail and the outbox stay on the database because they need transactions.  the opt-in `Rask.Cache` package — a developer-facing cache on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). Implements the standard `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Distributed.IDistributedCache` (Get/Set/Refresh/Remove + sync/async, `DistributedCacheEntryOptions` absolute/AbsoluteRelativeToNow/sliding) via `RaskDistributedCache<TContext>` — stores one `CacheEntry` row per key (Key PK, Value byte[], AbsoluteExpiration?, SlidingSeconds?, effective ExpiresAt, CreatedAt) through IDbContextFactory; a read past ExpiresAt is a MISS + lazily evicted, a read of a sliding entry RENEWS ExpiresAt (capped by any absolute deadline). Plus a typed `ICache`/`Cache` layer over it: `GetOrCreateAsync<T>(key, factory, options?)` (factory runs once on a miss — not a lock, keep it idempotent), `GetAsync<T>`, `SetAsync<T>`, `RemoveAsync`, serializing T with System.Text.Json; the reflection overloads are `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]`/`[RequiresDynamicCode]` and have trim-safe `JsonTypeInfo<T>` siblings (the byte[] IDistributedCache surface is fully trim-safe). The hosted `CachePurger<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer) bulk-deletes rows past ExpiresAt on PurgeInterval (default 5min) via ExecuteDeleteAsync — a transient DB error (SQLITE_BUSY) is caught per sweep so it never faults the host. Wire: `services.AddRaskCache<AppDbContext>(o => { o.PurgeInterval; o.DefaultSlidingExpiration; })` (registers IDistributedCache + ICache + the purger, idempotent) + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskCache()` in OnModelCreating (maps CacheEntry) + `rask db add AddCache && rask db update`. Server-side; one purger per app; no source generator, no Rask.Cqrs dependency. Drops into ASP.NET session state (`AddSession()`) and anything else built on IDistributedCache. No `rask generate` verb (there's no per-instance artifact to scaffold).
- [Batteries dashboard](docs/dashboard.md): the opt-in `Rask.Dashboard` package — an operator dashboard at `/_ops` over every DB-backed pillar's own table, no exporter or second datastore. `builder.Services.AddRaskDashboard<AppDbContext>()` (scaffolded by `rask new --ops`, included in `--all-batteries`) mounts a route chain under a `[Route("_ops")]` layout. Panels: Overview (a tile per queue + a banner the moment any dead letter exists), Queues (outbox/jobs/mail in one view split due/delayed/FAILED/processed, expand a row for its last error + stored payload), Cache (keys, sizes, expiry, expired-not-yet-swept), Logs (bounded in-memory tail of the ILogger pipeline — memory-only, gone on restart — plus, when `Rask.Logging` is registered, a **History** mode reading its durable store: paged with level/category/text filters; two modes rather than a merged view because that store's writer flushes on an interval), System (SQLite pragmas read live via the open DbConnection, DB size, recurring-job schedule joined to RecurringJobState). A panel appears ONLY when its battery is BOTH registered (its options singleton resolves) AND mapped (Model.FindEntityType) — the second half catches AddRaskX() without modelBuilder.AddRaskX(), where the service resolves but every query throws. FAILED = `ProcessedAt IS NULL AND Attempts >= MaxAttempts`, the inverse of the processors' drain query (there is no status column). SECURITY IS FAIL-CLOSED: pages carry `[Authorize(Policy = RaskDashboardPolicies.Access)]` on the LAYOUT (RouteAuthorizationGuard walks the chain, so it covers every page + re-checks on in-app nav); the default policy is installed with PostConfigure<AuthorizationOptions> so call order is irrelevant and an app-defined policy always wins — undefined => open in Development (with a banner) and DENY-ALL everywhere else. ACTIONS `o.Actions` (default Safe): retry a dead letter / retry all / purge processed / evict a cache key; `RaskDashboardActions.All` adds delete-a-row and flush-the-cache. Each is ONE ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete with the guard in the WHERE clause (never a tracked entity), so the DB evaluates it at write time and the dashboard can't raise a concurrency exception; the retry guard is the inverse of the drain query, so a row in flight is invisible to it and retry is safe against a live queue with no coordination. Panels poll `RefreshInterval` (2s), compare before re-rendering (idle => no diff, no WS traffic), and the loop is BOUNDED by `MaxPollDuration` (5min, then a Resume button) because every open tab competes for SQLite's single write lock. Backup tiles are opt-in via `IDashboardBackupProbe` — referencing Rask.SQLite.Snapshots/Litestream would drag a native SQLitePCLRaw provider bundle into every consumer and tie a provider-agnostic EF dashboard to SQLite. Also adds `BsStat` to Rask.Bootstrap (tone colours the value, not the card).
- [Background jobs](docs/jobs.md): the opt-in `Rask.Jobs` package — durable background work on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). A job is a `IJob` (: Rask.Cqrs ICommand) run off the request thread by an ordinary `ICommandHandler<TJob>`. Inject `IJobQueue` and `EnqueueAsync(job)` (run asap) / `ScheduleAsync(job, delay|runAt)` (delayed) — writes one `Job` row (Type name + JSON payload + RunAt) via IDbContextFactory (its OWN transaction — not atomic with a business change; use Rask.Outbox for that). The hosted `JobProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) claims due jobs (ProcessedAt==null && Attempts<MaxAttempts && RunAt<=now, oldest first, BatchSize), dispatches each via IDispatcher.DispatchAsync((ICommand)job) in a fresh scope, stamps ProcessedAt; on failure Attempts++/Error and pushes RunAt out by exponential backoff (BaseRetryDelay×2^(n-1) capped at MaxRetryDelay) up to MaxAttempts (default 25) → then a dead letter kept for inspection; completed jobs purged after RetentionPeriod (default 7d, Zero=keep). Durable interval-recurring: `o.AddRecurring<T>(name, every, factory)` enqueues a fresh job per interval, tracked in a RecurringJobState table so a restart never double-runs it (single catch-up if overdue); read the schedule back from `JobOptions.RecurringJobs` (public `RecurringJobDefinition` Name/Interval/Factory) and join it to RecurringJobState for last-fired, or call Factory() to enqueue an off-schedule run. Each job's outcome is saved on its OWN SaveChanges (not once per batch), so a row edited/deleted underneath the drain costs that one row instead of re-running everything the batch already executed; a failing poll is logged and retried rather than faulting the BackgroundService (which would stop the host). A source generator registers each IJob type (name→Type) at module load for reflection-free rehydration. Wire: `services.AddRaskCqrs()` + `services.AddRaskJobs<AppDbContext>(o => { PollInterval; MaxAttempts; AddRecurring(...); })` + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskJobs()` in OnModelCreating (maps Job + RecurringJobState) + `rask db add AddJobs && rask db update`. Server-side; one processor per app. `rask generate job <Name>` (alias `g j`) scaffolds the IJob record + handler.
- [Transactional email](docs/mail.md): the opt-in `Rask.Mail` package — durable transactional email queued on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). Compose with a fluent `Email` builder (`Email.To(addr,name?).AndTo/.Cc/.Bcc/.ReplyTo/.From/.Subject/.Body(Component|string html)/.PlainText/.Attach`); `.Body(Component)` renders a Rask component to HTML IMMEDIATELY (Component.ToHtml()) so the persisted row is self-contained (no source generator, no Rask.Cqrs dependency — nothing is rehydrated at send time). Addresses are validated at the call site (MimeKit MailboxAddress.TryParse) so a malformed address throws on build, not after MaxAttempts. Inject `IMailQueue` and `SendAsync(email)` (asap) / `ScheduleAsync(email, delay|runAt)` (delayed) — writes one `QueuedMail` row (envelope + already-rendered HTML) via IDbContextFactory, defaulting From from MailOptions. The hosted `MailProcessor<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer poll) claims due messages (ProcessedAt==null && Attempts<MaxAttempts && RunAt<=now, oldest first, BatchSize), delivers each via the registered `IMailSender` resolved per message from a fresh scope (so a custom scoped sender isn't captured), stamps ProcessedAt PER MESSAGE (a save failure re-sends at most that one, never the batch); on failure Attempts++/Error + exponential backoff (BaseRetryDelay×2^(n-1) capped MaxRetryDelay) up to MaxAttempts (default 10) → dead letter; a transient DB error (SQLITE_BUSY) is caught per cycle so it never faults the host; sent rows purged after RetentionPeriod (default 7d) via ExecuteDeleteAsync. `IMailSender` selection in AddRaskMail: `MailOptions.Smtp` set → `MailKitMailSender` (SMTP via MailKit); else `PickupDirectory` set → `PickupDirectoryMailSender` (writes .eml files); else `LogMailSender` — so it works ZERO-CONFIG in dev with no SMTP. Register your own IMailSender before AddRaskMail (any lifetime) to send via a provider API. Wire: `services.AddRaskMail<AppDbContext>(o => { o.From="..."; o.Smtp=new SmtpOptions{Host,Port,User,Password,Security}; o.PollInterval; o.MaxAttempts; })` + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskMail()` in OnModelCreating (maps QueuedMail) + `rask db add AddMail && rask db update`. References Rask.Core (Component.ToHtml) with PrivateAssets=all + MailKit; server-side; one processor per app; self-contained (no Rask.Jobs dependency). `rask generate email <Name>` (alias `g e`) scaffolds an email-body component AND auto-wires it: when it finds a single `DbContext` in the project (or `--context <Name>`) it registers `AddRaskMail<Ctx>` in Program.cs and adds `modelBuilder.AddRaskMail()` to that context's OnModelCreating (idempotent), leaving only SMTP config + `rask db add/update`; with no context (or several, no flag) it prints the manual steps instead.
- [Logging](docs/logging.md): the opt-in `Rask.Logging` package — a DURABLE log store in a SQLite file of its OWN (not the app's DbContext, no EF Core, no migration). `builder.Services.AddRaskLogging(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Logs") ?? "Data Source=logs.db", o => {...})` — scaffolded by `rask new --logs` (and included in `--all-batteries`); it takes a CONNECTION STRING rather than a `TContext`, which is the whole design: log lines arrive at machine rates and would put a high-frequency writer on the app database's single SQLite write lock, and the most valuable line is the one written WHILE A TRANSACTION IS FAILING — on the app's context that line rolls back with the failure. Trade-off, stated in the docs: `logs.db` is NOT covered by `rask db backup` or Litestream, and log lines can contain secrets. Registers a `[ProviderAlias("Rask")] ILoggerProvider` (via TryAddEnumerable, so a repeated call can't double-capture), so it sees exactly what every other sink sees — including the framework's `Rask.Live`/`Rask.Diff`/`Rask.Lifecycle` categories. PATH: a log call formats and `TryWrite`s into a bounded `Channel` (`BoundedChannelFullMode.DropWrite`, `QueueCapacity` 10_000) — it NEVER blocks or throws on the caller's thread; a full buffer DROPS the entry and counts it. The hosted `LogWriter` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer on `FlushInterval` 1s) drains it and inserts up to `BatchSize` (500) rows in ONE `ExecuteInImmediateTransactionAsync` (Rask.SQLite's non-blocking, thread-yielding busy-retry) with a single re-bound prepared command; `StopAsync` drains what's buffered under `ShutdownDrainTimeout` (5s) before completing the channel, because the lines just before a shutdown are the ones worth keeping. RETENTION every `PurgeInterval` (1h): entries older than `Retention` (14d, `TimeSpan.Zero` = forever) then a trim to the newest `MaxRows` (100_000, 0 = uncapped) — BOTH by default, since age alone can't bound the disk under a storm; deleted in pages of 1000 looping until drained, so the write lock is never held for a whole sweep. SCHEMA is `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS RaskLog` (Id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY — a rowid alias, deliberately NOT AUTOINCREMENT; Timestamp TEXT round-trip "O" UTC so range filters are string compares and the file reads in a sqlite3 shell; Level INTEGER; Category; EventId; Message; Exception) + 3 indexes, created once behind a SemaphoreSlim, with the production pragmas (WAL matters: it's what lets the dashboard read while the writer flushes) applied on EVERY open. RE-ENTRANCY: `Rask.Logging*` and `Microsoft.Data.Sqlite*` are ALWAYS excluded from capture whatever `o.ExcludedCategories` says — otherwise a SQLite failure logs a line that fails to write that logs a line. `o.MinimumLevel` is a FLOOR, not an override (the pipeline applies `Logging:LogLevel` first). READ IT with `ILogStore`: `QueryAsync(LogQuery{MinimumLevel, Category, Search, From, To, Page, PageSize})` → `LogPage(Entries newest-first, TotalCount, Page, PageSize, PageCount)`, plus `CategoriesAsync`/`CountAsync`/`PurgeAsync`/`ClearAsync`; LIKE wildcards in user text are escaped, so searching `100%` means a literal percent. METRICS on meter `Rask.Logging`: `rask.logs.written`, `rask.logs.dropped` (THE ONE TO ALERT ON — a full buffer OR a batch whose write failed; it is the only signal that the stored log is incomplete), `rask.logs.purged`, `rask.logs.stored` (sampled by the writer, not per observation). `rask deploy` sets `ConnectionStrings__Logs=Data Source=/data/logs.db` on the same volume as app.db. In `Rask.Dashboard`, `/_ops/logs` gains a **History** mode (paged, level/category/text filters) beside the always-present in-memory **Live** tail — two modes rather than a merged view because the writer flushes on an interval, so the newest lines are buffered but not yet on disk. Scopes are not captured (`BeginScope` returns null). Trim/AOT safe: no reflection, no serializer.
- [Cache](docs/cache.md): the opt-in `Rask.Cache` package — a developer-facing cache on the app's own EF Core database (no broker/Redis). Implements the standard `Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Distributed.IDistributedCache` (Get/Set/Refresh/Remove + sync/async, `DistributedCacheEntryOptions` absolute/AbsoluteRelativeToNow/sliding) via `RaskDistributedCache<TContext>` — stores one `CacheEntry` row per key (Key PK, Value byte[], AbsoluteExpiration?, SlidingSeconds?, effective ExpiresAt, CreatedAt) through IDbContextFactory; a read past ExpiresAt is a MISS + lazily evicted, a read of a sliding entry RENEWS ExpiresAt (capped by any absolute deadline). Plus a typed `ICache`/`Cache` layer over it: `GetOrCreateAsync<T>(key, factory, options?)` (factory runs once on a miss — not a lock, keep it idempotent), `GetAsync<T>`, `SetAsync<T>`, `RemoveAsync`, serializing T with System.Text.Json; the reflection overloads are `[RequiresUnreferencedCode]`/`[RequiresDynamicCode]` and have trim-safe `JsonTypeInfo<T>` siblings (the byte[] IDistributedCache surface is fully trim-safe). The hosted `CachePurger<TContext>` (BackgroundService, PeriodicTimer) bulk-deletes rows past ExpiresAt on PurgeInterval (default 5min) via ExecuteDeleteAsync — a transient DB error (SQLITE_BUSY) is caught per sweep so it never faults the host. Wire: `services.AddRaskCache<AppDbContext>(o => { o.PurgeInterval; o.DefaultSlidingExpiration; })` (registers IDistributedCache + ICache + the purger, idempotent) + register the context as IDbContextFactory + `modelBuilder.AddRaskCache()` in OnModelCreating (maps CacheEntry) + `rask db add AddCache && rask db update`. Server-side; one purger per app; no source generator, no Rask.Cqrs dependency. Drops into ASP.NET session state (`AddSession()`) and anything else built on IDistributedCache. No `rask generate` verb (there's no per-instance artifact to scaffold).
- [Mobile & PWA](docs/pwa.md): build installable mobile apps in C#. WASM = full PWA (install, true offline, push, every device API). Server = installable + push-capable via AddRaskPwa (serves manifest + service worker, auto-registers it, emits the manifest link into the server-rendered head), but NOT an offline app (offline navigations show a static offline.html; no background sync; install-prompt + activation-bound device APIs stay WASM-only). Typed Web app manifest (WebAppManifest in Rask.Core.Browser; WASM UsePwa / Server AddRaskPwa), default service worker (rask-sw.js; shared push/notificationclick handlers in Rask.Core), IWebPush + INotifications + IBadge + IWakeLock (Rask.Core.Browser, both hosts), `rask new MyApp --template wasm --pwa` / `rask new MyApp --pwa`. Sending push from the backend: the opt-in `Rask.WebPush` package (IWebPushSender, VAPID RFC 8292 + aes128gcm RFC 8291, zero external deps) — full reference in [Web Push](docs/webpush.md).
- [Web Push (server send)](docs/webpush.md): the opt-in Rask.WebPush package delivers a Web Push notification from your backend, zero external deps. VapidKeys.Generate() mints a base64url P-256 pair (RFC 8292; PublicKey IS the browser's applicationServerKey, hand the same string to the client IWebPush.SubscribeAsync); AddRaskWebPush(o => { o.VapidKeys; o.Subject = mailto:/https: }) validates at startup; store the client's PushSubscription(Endpoint, P256dh, Auth); IWebPushSender.SendAsync(sub, WebPushMessage.Text(title, body, url)) returns a WebPushResult (IsSuccess; ShouldDelete on 404/410 — prune it; ShouldRetry on 429/5xx). Typed WebPushMessage fields serialize to the default rask-sw.js JSON {title,body,icon,badge,tag,data.url}; RawPayload is the escape hatch; Urgency/Ttl/Topic map to RFC 8030 semantics; payloads encrypted with aes128gcm (RFC 8291). Standalone server library — no Rask.Core/Rask.Wasm dependency.
- [Native mobile (iOS/Android)](docs/native.md): the `Rask.Native` WebView-hybrid host — run a Rask app natively on iOS/Android inside a platform WebView, driven by the SAME render/diff pipeline as Server/WASM (it subclasses LiveSessionBase). Two modes: Native+Local (in-process, offline — `NativeAppHost.RunLocalAsync<App>`) and Native+Server (thin native shell over a remote Rask Server — `ConnectToServer`). The platform WebView is abstracted behind the `INativeWebView` bridge (WKWebView on iOS / android.webkit.WebView on Android), implemented in the app head, so the library builds/unit-tests on plain net10.0 with no iOS/Android workloads. Ships the native client dialect (rask.native.js) + boot shell. Scaffold + run: `rask new MyApp --template native`, then `dotnet workload install ios android` and `dotnet build -t:Run -f net10.0-android` (or `-f net10.0-ios`). The `native` template (shared components + Platforms/iOS WKWebView head + Platforms/Android WebView head) ships and runs end-to-end on both platforms; the template's App.cs pads Body by `env(safe-area-inset-*)` (with a viewport-fit=cover viewport) so content clears the notch/status bar. The native client shares the transport-neutral DOM helpers (rAF input/scroll coalescing, keyboard + drag, scoped-CSS FOUC gating) with the Server/WASM clients via common spliced modules (rask-input.js/rask-scoped.js/rask-events.js). The RUNNABLE native showcase is two examples mirroring the Server/WASM pairing, both mounting the SAME Rask.Example.Shared.App: `samples/Rask.Example.Native` (Native + Local, in-process — the peer of the WASM sample) and `samples/Rask.Example.Native.Server` (Native + Server, a thin shell over a remote Rask.Example.Server — the peer of the Server sample). Both multi-target net10.0-ios;net10.0-android, so they sit OUTSIDE Rask.slnx and are compile-gated by a dedicated macOS `native` CI job across every project × TFM; `-t:Run -f net10.0-android|net10.0-ios`. On-device E2E is Appium (tests/Rask.Native.Appium.Tests): Appium installs + drives the REAL app on an Android emulator / iOS simulator, switches into the WebView, and asserts the showcase rendered with scoped CSS + Bootstrap (served through NativeOriginAssets) — run in the macOS `native-appium` CI job (boots the emulator, `appium --allow-insecure=uiautomator2:chromedriver_autodownload`, EmbedAssembliesIntoApk APK). This replaced the old Playwright-in-Chromium headless shim (which masked a real device-only bug: the boot shell loads at /index.native.html, a path NativeOriginAssets now serves). To serve a FULL app's assets on-device (not just the two boot files), Rask.Native provides `NativeOriginAssets.Resolve(path, readStaticFile)` (the origin request table: boot shell + client, scoped /_rask/a/* from ScopedAssetRegistry, and your wwwroot/Bootstrap/data via a caller-supplied bundled-asset reader — Android AssetManager / iOS NSBundle) + `NativeAssetHttpHandler` (serves the in-process demo HttpClient from the same table so data/*.json works offline). Native header & footer: a native page is a COMPOSED tree — the native bars (`NativeHeaderBar`/`NativeTabBar`/`NativeToolbar`) as siblings of a `NativeWebView` that hosts the ordinary page shell (Doctype/Html/Head/Body). They are ordinary factory-built components in `Rask.Native.Components` (all inherit `NativeComponent : Component`, composed in `Render()`, NOT base-class slots), with type-safe `NativeIcon` SF-Symbol/drawable pairs + `Features.Routes.*` tabs. The platform head implements `INativeChrome` (registered like `IShare`, assign `webView.ChromeView`) and projects the bars to a real UINavigationBar+UITabBar/UIToolbar (iOS) / top+bottom bars (Android), serializing the NativeWebView's HTML into the WebView between them. Bars render NO HTML — nesting one inside the HTML (an element child, or inside NativeWebView content) is a RASK032 compile error; bars are collected during the render walk (DI-correct, last of a kind wins), pushed with a byte noop-guard, button taps run OnClick + tabs navigate. Style the bars with `NativeColor` (the color sibling of NativeIcon: Hex/Rgba/Adaptive(light,dark)/System) — per-bar `Background`/`Tint`/`TitleColor` (+ tab-bar `UnselectedTint`) or an app-wide `NativeTheme` on host.Services; per-bar wins, then theme, then the platform default (unset keeps the OS look; adaptive colors track dark mode). The Android head resolves each NativeIcon drawable so tabs/buttons show real icons. NativeTab takes an optional `Badge` string (unread count) → UITabBarItem.BadgeValue (iOS) / icon overlay (Android); bind it to live state and it updates on the next render. NativeHeaderBar takes optional `Segments` (2–3 labels, shown in place of the title) → UISegmentedControl titleView (iOS) / button row (Android), controlled via `SelectedSegment` + `OnSegmentChanged(int)` (reuses nativeTap dispatch). A `NativeMenuButton` bar item (with `NativeMenuItem` entries: Title/Icon/OnClick/Destructive) opens a native overflow pull-down → UIMenu (iOS) / PopupMenu (Android), reusing nativeTap dispatch. A `NativeBackButton` (header Leading) pops WebView history like hardware Back (the initial render replaces the boot shell URL in history so Back lands on the app's first screen). Sharing an app web+native? Branch on the host via `IsNative`/`IsServer`/`IsWasm`/`IsIOS`/`IsAndroid` (+ the `HostShell`/`HostEngine`/`HostPlatform` enums, three orthogonal render-cache-safe axes): compose the native tree under `IsNative`, render a web `BsNavbar` on Server/WASM. Preview / pre-1.0: native device backends (native push/biometrics) are the main remaining follow-up (the scoped-JS invoke gate + file uploads also stay host-specific for now). WebView hybrid (C# runs native, view is a WebView) — HTML in a WebView plus the one bounded native header/footer surface, not a general native-control renderer.
- [Authentication](docs/authentication.md): cookie/JWT, Authorize, route guards.
- [Observability](docs/observability.md): structured logging, the `Rask.Server` meter + activity source, `AddRaskLiveSessions()` health check.
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): `RaskLiveOptions` (shared: diff mode, path base, session cap) + `RaskServerOptions` (server-only WS/grace/idle/backpressure limits) + `RaskUploadOptions` (upload size + per-session quota), appsettings binding + startup validation.
- [Deployment](docs/deployment.md): containerizing the apps — opt-in `--docker` on the three web templates scaffolds a production multi-stage Dockerfile (+ `.dockerignore`): the `server` and `wasm-hosted` templates build on the .NET SDK image and run on `aspnet:10.0` (non-root, port 8080, `UseHttpsRedirection` no-ops in-container so terminate TLS at the proxy and forward the WebSocket upgrade); the standalone `wasm` bundle publishes then serves from `nginx:alpine` with a bundled `nginx.conf` (SPA `try_files` fallback, `application/wasm` MIME, `gzip_static` for the baked `*.gz`). `native` is a mobile app (app-store package, not a container). GitHub Pages / sub-path via `/p:RaskPathBase=`. One-command deploy of that Dockerfile: `rask deploy --host root@box [--domain app.example.com]` builds the image on the box over SSH and runs it — with `--domain` a shared Caddy proxy adds automatic HTTPS and deploys are zero-downtime (blue-green), multiple apps to one host. Point it at a **bare VPS** (root + SSH key, nothing else) and it prepares the box first — Docker, a non-root `deploy` login, ufw, SSH hardening — after showing the plan and asking once, so you never SSH in yourself; `rask deploy --github-actions` writes the workflow that repeats it on every push. Note ufw does **not** filter Docker-published ports (docker writes its own iptables rules): that's benign here because the only published ports are the intended-public ones (Caddy's 80/443, or `--port`), but an unrelated `-p` container won't be hidden by `ufw deny`.
- [Accessibility](docs/accessibility.md): ARIA via the `Aria` dictionary, `Role`/`TabIndex`, the `Img` alt-text analyzer (RASK023), and automatic navigation a11y on the Server host (SPA route changes show a progress bar, move focus into the new page's `<main>`, and announce the route via `aria-live`).
- [Migration from Blazor](docs/migration-from-blazor.md): mapping Blazor concepts to Rask.
- [Diagnostics](docs/diagnostics.md): RASK001–035 compile-time diagnostics + fixes, including IDE quick-fixes (lightbulb) for RASK001 (add `required`) and RASK023 (insert `Alt: ""`), shipped in `Rask.Generators.CodeFixes`.
- [Testing](docs/testing.md): the `Rask.Testing` package (`RaskTest.Render(component)` → `RenderedComponent`; `.ClickAsync()`/`.InvokeAsync(handlerId, json?)` dispatch handlers + re-render; `.Html`/`.HandlerId`/`.Attr` query) for in-process component unit tests, plus Playwright E2E patterns.
